audio_segments.transcript: Hello, Marcus Tan. This is Rachel Lim from the bank, calling as requested. Is this still a convenient time for our conversation? I know you wanted to keep the telephone update brief.
Yes, now can. I'm back in the office, door closed already. Let me give you my particulars. My identification number is G eight three six four four seven nine M. My date of birth is 7 September 1965.
Thank you. I have your details. We can keep the conversation focused, and I will avoid unnecessary technical language.

For this transaction, I want Orion Global Income Fund. Use Japanese yen for this transaction. Last time I invested 1,000,000 Japanese yen, so funds aren't new to me. That was a previous investment, not today's amount. Just keep it practical, lah. Over the phone, long explanations quite hard to follow when people keep coming to my desk.

I recommend Orion Global Income Fund because it pools exposure across different bond issuers, rather than requiring you to select and monitor individual issuers yourself. That makes the investment process more manageable alongside running your business. Purely as an illustration, an allocation of 7,500,000 Japanese yen would give exposure to the fund's pooled holdings rather than a directly selected bond. That is an example, not your transaction amount.

All right, plain language is better. Recently I'm more involved in the family business again. Got deliveries, staff matters, all coming together. Even sitting down for a proper call takes some arranging.
That sounds like a busy return to the office. For future telephone updates, would you prefer that we arrange a convenient time by message rather than call unexpectedly?
Message first is better. Then I can step away from the warehouse floor. Otherwise the background so noisy, you talk and I also cannot hear properly. Today the office is quiet enough.

I will note that contact preference. Let me cover the disclosure now. For Orion Global Income Fund, rising interest rates can reduce the market value of the bonds it holds, which can bring down the fund's unit value. Do you understand how rising interest rates could bring down the value of your holding in this fund?
Yes, I understand. Rates go up, the bonds in the fund can drop in value, so my holding can drop also.
The transaction charge is 0.5% of the investment amount. You could lose some or all of the capital you invest in this fund.

For the current investment, the amount I'm committing is 100,000,000. The quantity I want is 2,000 units. I want to buy the units. Make it a market order, please. There's something else about the money. Some of the subscription money is customer receipts I deliberately kept outside the business accounts to hide where it came from. Put the investment under my personal name lah, so those receipts harder to trace.
Your instruction is to sell the units.
No, you got the direction wrong there. I want to buy the units.

I apologise for that error. With the direction corrected, please confirm your final instruction: buy 2,000 units of Orion Global Income Fund, for a total amount of 100,000,000 in Japanese yen, using a market order. Is that your instruction?
Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please go ahead with it.
Thank you for your time today, Marcus. I have noted your preference for arranging calls by message. I will leave you to get back to the office.
Thanks, Rachel. That helps with the interruptions. I need to get back to the staff now. Goodbye.
